2  MFA No. 5160 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 6434 of 2018 PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant as well as the insurer is in appeal.

2. The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.7,15,900/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.

3. The insurer contends that the attribution of negligence on the vehicle insured by it on the rider of the vehicle cannot be accepted, since it is not in dispute that the claimant suddenly came out of the road, as a result of which, the accident occurred.
4. It is also contended that the sums awarded towards 'loss of income during the period of treatment' was incorrect.

5. The claimant, on the other hand, contends that the loss of future income would have to be taken into consideration since the possibility of the claimant working after retirement would not disappear.

6. The evidence on record indicates that the chargesheet was filed against the driver of the bus,
which had been insured by the insurer.
This indicates that even according to the police the negligence was on the part of the driver of the bus.
7. The insurer has not examined the driver of the bus in order to establish that the claimant had also contributed to the accident.
In the light of these facts, the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the bus is responsible cannot be found fault with.
8. As far as compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the claimant did continue in his earlier avocation as cook in Gr.II / staff canteen and therefore, there was no loss of income.

The argument that the claimant could probably work even after retirement cannot be a ground to award compensation towards 'loss of future income' because after retirement he would be entitled to pension.
It is, therefore, clear that denial of loss of future income cannot be found fault with.

9. The argument that compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during laid-up period' cannot also be accepted since the evidence on record indicates that the claimant had received M/S Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri C N Manjunath on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193927070/
3 salary by commuting leave of 70 days.

sentences.text: The Tribunal after taking into consideration this fact has awarded a sum of Rs.2,19,324/- by considering the monthly gross salary at Rs.36,754/-, as indicated in the pay slip.
In my view, this award also cannot be found fault with.
10. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.60,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

11. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. As the claimant was hospitalised for about 27 days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.40,000/- towards 'food, nutrition and attendant charges'.
13. The sums awarded towards medical expenses and future medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence, does not call for modification and hence confirmed.

14. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
 Sl. Particulars Award by Award by  No. Tribunal this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)

1 . Pain and agony 60,000/- 1,00,000/-
 2. Loss of income during 2,19,324/- 2,19,324/-
treatment period

3. Medical expenses 3,56,539/- 3,56,539/-
 4. Loss of amenities 50,000/- 1,50,000/-
 5.

Future medical 30,000/- 30,000/-
 expenses

6. Conveyance, food - 40,000/-
 nourishment and  attendant charges  Total 7,15,893/- 8,95,863/-
15.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.8,95,900/- (rounded off) as against Rs.7,15,900/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

17. On such deposit, 70% of the compensation amount is ordered to be invested in the name of claimant for a period of five years in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of his choice with liberty to withdraw the interest accrued thereon periodically renewable for another period of three years.
After maturity, the Bank shall release the amount in favour of claimant without any further proceedings.
The remaining 30% of the compensation amount shall be released in favour of claimant through account payee cheque after proper identification.
18. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
19. The appeal filed by insurer is dismissed and the appeal filed by claimant is accordingly allowed in part.
